review: 1:3–4 the precious blood for a sinner like me keeps 1 Pet 1:19 (דָּם יָקָר) and the Hebrew order 'blood … for a sinner', so the stanza's wonder lands on the last word as the Arabic's مِنْ أَجْلِي does.
2:3 יָרַדְתָּ מִמְּרוֹם שָׁמַיִם — the Arabic نَزَلْتَ مِنْ أَوْجِ السَّمَا keeps the descent; the Hebrew uses יָרַד, the verb of Exod 19:20 and Eph 4:9, rather than a modern 'באת מן'.

3:3–4 לְעֻמַּת … כְּאַיִן הִיא — the Arabic إِزَاءَ حُبِّكَ لَا شَيْء is 'beside Your love it is nothing'; לְעֻמַּת (Exod 25:37, 'over against') keeps the comparison side-by-side instead of saying 'my love is small'.

5:1 קַיֶּם־נָא — the Arabic فَأَنْجِزَنَّ carries an energetic imperative; the Hebrew keeps the force with the entreating נָא of Gen 50:17 rather than a bare imperative, so the line is a plea and not a claim.

6:1–4 the threefold 'He loved me' is kept with the same verb three times (אֲהֵבַנִי), as the Arabic repeats أَحَبَّنِي, and the stanza closes on the same 'for me' as stanza 1 so the hymn ends where it began.
